claim: The current frozen 4-class detector reduces false-elephant alarms on external multi-animal scenes without elephants relative to the original elephant-only detector.
evidence: false-elephant image rate 0.509934 -> 0.145695; paired delta comparator-selective=0.364238; 95% CI [0.278146, 0.450331]

claim: The current frozen 4-class detector maintains elephant sensitivity while reducing false alarms.
The current frozen 4-class detector is overall superior to the original elephant-only detector.
The current frozen 4-class detector significantly reduces animal-confuser to elephant overlap errors in positive mixed scenes.
The 9-image elephant+lion supplement establishes broad in-vocabulary mixed-species robustness.
evidence: selective elephant recall=0.444444, comparator recall=0.888889; lion-to-elephant overlap errors=4 for selective and 4 for comparator

claim: Elephant-class filtering itself is the main reason for the lower negative-scene alarm rate.
evidence: 4-class any-class negative alarm rate=0.158940; elephant-filtered rate=0.145695; difference is small compared with the detector-to-detector false-alarm difference

claim: R17 validates detector-to-tracker-to-forecast end-to-end operational performance.
evidence: R17 is an image-level detector/selective-filter robustness experiment only; the historical end-to-end limitation remains unchanged.

claim: The current 4-class detector should replace the original elephant-only detector in the present system.
evidence: False-alarm reduction is statistically supported, but sensitivity, recall, precision and F1 losses are statistically supported; therefore replacement is not justified.
